writeup.headline: Zscaler rates Hold: strong growth and net cash offset by high absolute valuation and GAAP losses.
writeup.thesis: Zscaler scores 58, a Hold, 7 points below the Buy band and 14 points above Sell. Growth is the main support, with TTM revenue growth of 25.4% and latest-quarter revenue growth of 24.9% year on year, though growth slowed by 0.6 pp from the previous quarter. The balance sheet scores 100 on net cash, with cash at 2.05 times debt. Quality is middling: a 76.8% gross margin and 25.4% FCF margin sit against a -4.0% operating margin, stock-based compensation at 24.5% of revenue and diluted share count up 3.8% year on year. Valuation weighs most: P/S of 12.4x and P/FCF of 48.9x are high in absolute terms and the FCF yield is 2.9 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield, even though the stock is cheap against its own history (P/S cheaper than at 48 of the last 61 month-ends, P/FCF near the middle of the last 61 month-ends (cheaper than at 37, more expensive than at 24)).
key_risks: High absolute multiples (12.4x sales, 48.9x FCF) leave little room if growth slows further.
Negative GAAP operating margin of -4.0% with stock-based compensation at 24.5% of revenue and ongoing dilution.
Volatile shares: down 39.2% from 12 months ago to 1 month ago and still 23.9% below the 52-week high after a sharp rebound.
Law firms have announced shareholder investigations, though no complaint has been filed.
Growth slowed by 0.6 pp from the previous quarter; continued deceleration would pressure the growth score.
what_would_change: Up to Buy (7 points): reaccelerating revenue growth, GAAP operating profitability, or a lower absolute valuation lifting the valuation score from 30.
Up: a filed complaint not materialising and stronger guidance would improve the news score from 54.
Down to Sell (14 points): a meaningful growth slowdown combined with a reversal of the recent price trend, which currently sits 53.5% above its 200-day average.
Down: a filed shareholder lawsuit or a guidance cut would hurt the news score.
